import itertools

# --- design structure -----------------------------------------------------------------

FAC = D.rsm_factors(UO)                       # load, elution_ph, flow, end_collect
PRM = {f: CFG.unit_op(UO).param(f) for f in FAC}
SP = {f: PRM[f].setpoint for f in FAC}
NOR = {f: PRM[f].nor for f in FAC}
CHR = {f: PRM[f].prange for f in FAC}

cen_scr = D.center_cv_df(UO, "screening").set_index("Response")
LAB = D.RESP_LABEL


def cv(resp, kind="rsm"):
    t = cen_rsm if kind == "rsm" else cen_scr
    return float(t.loc[LAB[resp], "%CV"])


def cmean(resp, kind="rsm"):
    t = cen_rsm if kind == "rsm" else cen_scr
    return float(t.loc[LAB[resp], "Mean"])


def nrep(resp, kind="rsm"):
    t = cen_rsm if kind == "rsm" else cen_scr
    return int(t.loc[LAB[resp], "n"])


def eff(resp, term, col="Effect"):
    d = D.screening_effects_df(UO, resp)
    return float(d[d["Term"] == term][col].iloc[0])


def coef(resp, term, col="Coef."):
    d = D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, resp)
    return float(d[d["Term"] == term][col].iloc[0])

def at(resp, **nat):

def box(resp, edges):

hcp_chain = pd.DataFrame({

# --- observed (model-free) leached Protein A record ------------------------------------

lpa_obs_max = float(max(d["leached_protein_a_ppm"].max() for d in _doe.values()))
lpa_scr = D.screening_effects_df(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm")

lpa_par_ph = D.par_nor_propagated(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm", "elution_ph")["par_nat"][1]

# --- analytical method performance ------------------------------------------------------
_meth = csv("dev_methods.csv").set_index("id")

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

Protein A chromatography is the capture step of the A-Mab drug-substance process and the
first chromatographic unit operation in the purification train. The step binds the antibody
from clarified harvest on an immobilised Protein A resin, washes the bound product, and
elutes it at low pH into the viral inactivation step that follows. It sets one quality
attribute of its own, leached Protein A, and it is the principal clearance step for host
cell protein (HCP) and residual DNA. The studies reported here executed the design
prospectively defined in the paired plan (PCP-005) on a qualified scale-down model, under
the lifecycle approach to process
validation [@fda2011] and the enhanced development approach of ICH Q8, Q9 and Q11
[@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11], and follow the A-Mab case study for the process model and the
criticality framework [@amab2009].

The step carries `{python} f"{n_param_step}"` process parameters. Four of them were studied
multivariately (protein load, elution buffer pH, load flow rate and end of pool collect) in
a `{python} f"{n_scr}"`-run two-level screening design followed by a `{python} f"{n_rsm}"`-run
face-centred response-surface design. The remaining two, operating temperature and bed
height, were assessed outside the multivariate design. `{python} f"{n_wccpp}"` parameters
are classified as well-controlled critical process parameters, `{python} f"{n_kpp}"` as key
process parameters and `{python} f"{n_gpp}"` as general process parameters. No parameter at
this step required designation as a critical process parameter.

Pool host cell protein and step yield are well described by the response-surface models,
with coefficients of determination of
`{python} f"{fit_rsm['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['R2']:.3f}"` and
`{python} f"{fit_rsm['step_yield']['R2']:.3f}"`. Pool host cell protein rises with protein
load and falls as elution buffer pH rises, and the two factors interact. Leached Protein A
behaves differently. No process parameter had a significant effect on it, and the fitted
surface predicts a run it has not seen no better than the mean of the response does, so the
study reports the attribute as robust to the operating parameters over the ranges studied and
does not treat its model as predictive. All `{python} f"{n_pools}"` pools assayed across the two designs
met the acceptance criterion of `{python} f"{lpa_acc_hi:g}"` ppm, the highest single
determination being `{python} f"{lpa_obs_max:.2f}"` ppm.

At drug substance the three impurity attributes this step governs all clear their limits
with margin. Host cell protein is the tightest of them, at a process capability index of
`{python} f"{cpk_hcp:.2f}"` against a mean of `{python} f"{hcp_ds_mean:.1f}"` ng/mg and a
limit of `{python} f"{hcp_acc_hi:g}"` ng/mg. The tightest capability in the drug-substance
process is not at this step; it is `{python} f"{min_cpk:.2f}"`, and it belongs to a viral
clearance attribute characterized in PCR-008 and PCR-009. No viral clearance is claimed for
Protein A chromatography, and no aggregate reduction is claimed either. The pool host cell
protein handed forward is not judged against the drug-substance specification, because the
polishing steps reported in PCR-007 and PCR-008 carry that reduction.

`{python} f"{n_dev}"` deviations were recorded during execution. Both were investigated,
impact-assessed and resolved without changing any parameter classification or the operating
region defined in §6 (both are described in §13). This report supports the transfer scope in
PTP-001 and rolls up into the master report PCMR-001.

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized immunoglobulin G subclass 1 monoclonal antibody whose principal
mechanism of action is antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. Its drug substance is
produced by fed-batch cell culture followed by a platform purification train of affinity
capture, low-pH viral inactivation, two polishing chromatography steps, small-virus
retentive filtration and formulation by ultrafiltration and diafiltration. The train and the
principal role of each step are given below (@tbl-train).

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(process_steps_df())
print()
print(": The A-Mab drug-substance process train and the principal role of each step. {#tbl-train}")
```

Protein A chromatography is operated in bind and elute mode. Clarified harvest is loaded on
an immobilised Protein A resin, which binds the antibody through its Fc region while the
bulk of the process impurities (host cell protein, DNA and media-derived small molecules)
pass to the flow-through and the wash. A low-pH elution buffer releases the product into a
pool that feeds the low-pH viral inactivation step directly, so the elution condition is
shared between two unit operations. Small quantities of Protein A ligand are released from
the resin during elution and enter the pool, so the step sets the leached Protein A
attribute and does not clear it.

The affinity mechanism is selective for the Fc region and is not sensitive to the glycan or
charge state of the molecule. Glycosylation and charge variants are formed in the production
bioreactor (PCR-003) and pass through capture unchanged, so they were not carried as
responses in this study. Aggregate also passes through. Aggregate reduction is credited to
cation exchange chromatography (PCR-007).

## Objectives

The study had five objectives.

- Quantify the effect of each multivariate parameter on pool host cell protein, step yield
  and leached Protein A across the characterization ranges.
- Define the multivariate operating region within which the quality attribute the step sets
  remains within its acceptance criterion.
- Establish proven acceptable ranges for each governed attribute and parameter, both at
  set-point and with the other parameters varying within their normal operating ranges.
- Classify every parameter of the step against the decision logic for parameter
  classification (SOP-4001).
- Justify the Stage 2 ranges and the step's contribution to the drug-substance control
  strategy.

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The report is a Stage 1 process design record under the lifecycle approach to process
validation [@fda2011]. It follows the enhanced development approach of ICH Q8 for design
space and parameter criticality, ICH Q9 for the risk basis of the study scope, and ICH Q11
for the link between process understanding and the control strategy
[@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11]. Criticality is treated as a continuum and not as a binary
classification, so an attribute of low to moderate criticality such as leached Protein A is
characterized and controlled even though it is not a release-limiting attribute. The process
model, the impurity behaviour of each unit operation and the criticality framework are taken
from the A-Mab case study [@amab2009].

ICH Q5A is not invoked for this step. Affinity capture can be shown to remove enveloped
virus, but no viral clearance claim is made here, and the cumulative clearance claim rests on
the low-pH hold, anion exchange and small-virus retentive filtration. Those three steps are
reported in PCR-006, PCR-008 and PCR-009 and are consolidated in PCMR-001. The documents
that frame or receive this report are listed below (@tbl-related).

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Platform and prior-product knowledge

The A-Mab purification process is a platform process with an extensive performance history.
Affinity capture on Protein A resin has been used at commercial scale for three previous
humanized IgG1 antibodies (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab) and through A-Mab clinical supply, with
essentially unchanged column chemistry, buffer system and cycle structure. That experience
establishes the mechanism of the step and the qualitative direction of every parameter
effect, so the purpose of this characterization was to confirm and bound those effects for
A-Mab, not to discover them. Prior knowledge was used to set the factor ranges and the
mechanistic expectations stated below; it was not used in place of data for any conclusion
in §5.

Four mechanistic expectations framed the design. Higher protein load increases the mass of
antibody bound per unit resin volume, and the host cell protein that co-adsorbs with the
product and elutes with it (both to the ligand and to the antibody itself) is expected to
rise in proportion, so pool host cell protein was expected to increase with load. A lower
elution pH is a harsher desorption condition that
releases more weakly associated host cell protein together with the product, so pool host
cell protein was expected to fall as elution buffer pH rises. Higher load flow rate
shortens the residence time available for binding and was expected to reduce step yield
through early breakthrough, most severely when the column is also heavily loaded. Collecting
further into the trailing edge of the elution peak recovers more product and was expected to
raise step yield.

Leached Protein A was expected to be governed by the resin and its cycle history and not by
the operating parameters. Ligand release from a Protein A resin is driven by hydrolysis and
proteolysis of the immobilised ligand, which depend on the base matrix, the packing quality,
the sanitisation regime and the number of cycles the column has seen. Those variables are
controlled under the resin life-cycle procedure (SOP-2008) and were held constant across the
study. Prior campaign experience
with an alternate resin is recorded in RA-004, which concluded that independent
characterization would be required for any resin change and that no bridging from platform
data would be accepted.

## Quality attributes in scope

The step sets one quality attribute of its own, and that attribute is listed below with its
acceptance criterion and criticality (@tbl-cqa-set).

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_for(UO))
print()
print(": Quality attribute set by the Protein A step, with acceptance criterion and "
      "criticality assigned under the Tool #1 impact and uncertainty ranking. {#tbl-cqa-set}")
```

Leached Protein A is of low to moderate criticality. It is a process-derived impurity with
an immunogenicity rationale, and it has no direct efficacy or safety effect at the levels
reached; its acceptance criterion of `{python} f"{lpa_acc_hi:g}"` ppm applies at drug
substance. The attribute is introduced here and reduced by every subsequent chromatography
step, so this report gives the level the capture pool delivers and defers the cumulative
position to the capability section (§8) and to PCMR-001.

Two further attributes are governed but not set here. They are the process impurities the
capture step removes (@tbl-cqa-cleared).

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(["hcp", "residual_dna"]))
print()
print(": Quality attributes formed upstream and cleared by the Protein A step. {#tbl-cqa-cleared}")
```

Host cell protein is the larger of the two in characterization terms, because the capture
step delivers the single largest reduction of the purification train and because the pool
level it produces sets the impurity burden the polishing steps have to handle. Residual DNA
is of very low criticality and clears to well below its limit across the train. Neither
attribute is judged against its drug-substance criterion at the outlet of this step.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection

The scope of this study was set by the pre-characterization risk assessment RA-001. That
assessment ranked every parameter of the step on its potential main effect on quality
attributes and on its potential to interact with other parameters, and assigned a study type
from the combined score. Parameters with the highest combined scores were assigned to the
multivariate design, parameters with intermediate scores to univariate assessment, and
parameters whose ranges are fixed by equipment design or by an existing platform claim to no
new study.

Four parameters were assigned to the multivariate design. Protein load and elution buffer pH
were ranked highest because prior knowledge links both to pool host cell protein and because
they were expected to interact. Load flow rate and end of pool collect were included because
both act on step yield and because the flow rate effect was expected to depend on the load,
which is an interaction a univariate study cannot resolve. Operating temperature and bed
height were assigned to univariate assessment. Temperature acts on binding kinetics and is
held within a narrow band by the chromatography chamber, and bed height is fixed at packing
under SOP-2008 and verified before use (plate count and peak asymmetry).

The characterization ranges were set wider than the routine control ranges, at roughly twice
to three times the normal operating range for each factor, so that the study would define an
operating region with margin around the set-point instead of merely confirming the set-point
itself. The wider ranges also support later movement within the design space without new
studies. The ranges are given in the study design section (@tbl-params).

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

A laboratory-scale chromatography system was qualified as a model of the commercial-scale
Protein A step under SOP-1001, and all data in this report were generated on it. The model
was designed on the established principles of chromatography scaling. It uses the same resin
lot family, the same bed height as the commercial column, the same linear flow velocities,
and the same load, wash and elution volumes expressed in column volumes, so that residence
time and the number of column volumes at every phase of the cycle are preserved across
scales. Column efficiency was verified by plate count and peak asymmetry before each
sequence of runs.

Qualification compared the scale-down model against commercial-equivalent operation at the
set-point in triplicate, on the performance parameters that carry the step's claims (step
yield, elution pool volume, pool host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A). No
statistically significant difference was found between scales on any of these, so the model
is accepted as representative of the full-scale system for the purposes of this study. The
qualification data are held in the scale-down model qualification record filed under
SOP-1001 and are not reproduced here.

The warrant this places on the study is specific and worth stating in its bounds. Because
residence time, column volumes and bed height are matched, effects that act through binding
kinetics, mass transfer and peak position transfer between scales. Effects that would act
through wall support, packing heterogeneity or column-diameter-dependent flow distribution
are not reproduced at laboratory scale, and no claim in this report depends on them. The
operating region defined in §6 is therefore a claim about the scale-down model, verified at
commercial scale only at the set-point.

## Operation

Each run followed the cycle defined in SOP-2007. The column was equilibrated, loaded with
clarified harvest at the run's protein load and load flow rate, washed with the platform
wash sequence, and eluted with the run's elution buffer at the assigned pH. Pool collection
started on the ascending edge at the platform absorbance threshold and stopped at the run's
end of pool collect, expressed in column volumes from the start of elution. The column was
then stripped, sanitised and re-equilibrated under SOP-2008.

Inputs held to platform specification (resin lot, buffer compositions other than the elution
pH under study, wash sequence, equilibration conditions and column packing quality) were
controlled as identity and quality attributes and were not characterized. A single clarified
harvest pool at nominal titre and impurity burden was
used as feed for all runs, so that the measured effects are attributable to the operating
parameters alone. Feed-state variation was not a factor of this design, and §6 states the
bound that follows from that choice.

## Analytical methods

Every response was measured by a validated method. The controlled documents governing the
step and its analytics are listed below (@tbl-sop).

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=PROTEIN_A_SOP_REFS, amvs=PROTEIN_A_AMV_REFS))
print()
print(": Standard operating procedures and validated analytical methods applied to the "
      "Protein A characterization studies. {#tbl-sop}")
```

Pool host cell protein was determined by the platform host cell protein enzyme-linked
immunosorbent assay (AMV-3012) and is reported per unit of product mass, in ng/mg. Leached
Protein A was determined by a ligand-specific enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (AMV-3016)
and is reported in ppm relative to product mass. Step yield was calculated from product mass
in the pool against product mass in the load, using protein concentration by absorbance at
280 nm (AMV-3019). Residual DNA was determined by quantitative polymerase chain reaction
(AMV-3014) and size variants by size-exclusion chromatography (AMV-3011); neither was
carried as a response of the multivariate design, for the reasons given in §5.3 and §2.2.
Method performance for the assays that carry this step's claims is summarised in Appendix D.

## Sampling plan

Samples were drawn at the same points in every run. The load was sampled once for titre and
impurity burden, the flow-through and the wash were sampled for mass balance, and the
elution pool was sampled after mixing for all three responses. Strip fractions were retained
but were not assayed as part of this study. The retained pool aliquots were held frozen so
that any determination flagged during analytical review could be repeated on the same
material (see DEV-005-02).

The screening design carried `{python} f"{nrep('pool_hcp_ng_mg', 'screening')}"` centre-point
replicates and the response-surface design carried
`{python} f"{nrep('pool_hcp_ng_mg')}"`. Centre-point runs were executed at the set-point of
every factor, distributed through the run order and not grouped, so that the replicate
variation reflects the full range of day-to-day operation and not a single session.

## Statistical methods

All models were fitted on coded factors, with the set-point of each factor at coded zero and
the edges of its characterization range at coded minus one and plus one. For this step the
set-point of every multivariate factor coincides with the midpoint of its characterization
range, so coded zero and the set-point are the same condition. The screening model is an
ordinary least-squares fit of the main effects and all two-factor interactions, and an effect
is reported as twice the coded coefficient, which is the change in response across the full
range of that factor. The response-surface model is the full quadratic in the same four
factors.

Significance was assessed at the 5 % level. Model adequacy was judged on four statements
taken together (the coefficient of determination, the adjusted coefficient of determination,
the predicted coefficient of determination computed from the prediction error sum of squares,
and the lack-of-fit test against the centre-point pure error). The predicted coefficient of
determination is the decisive one for a predictive claim, because it measures how well the
fitted surface predicts an observation that was not used to fit it. A response for which no
factor is active and for which the lack-of-fit test is not significant is reported as robust,
and its model is retained as evidence of that robustness rather than used for prediction.

Commercial-scale capability was estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{n_mc:,}"` batches with every parameter of the train varying within its normal
operating range. Capability is expressed as a one-sided process capability index against the
relevant drug-substance limit. Proven acceptable ranges were computed from the fitted
response-surface model in two forms, described in §7.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space

The design covers the four parameters that the risk assessment linked to a quality attribute
or to process performance, across ranges that extend beyond the normal operating range in
both directions. The set-point, normal operating range and characterization range of every
parameter of the step are given in @tbl-params, together with the classification each
carries at the end of the study and the study type assigned to it by RA-001.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(report_params(UO))
print()
print(": Process parameters of the Protein A step, with set-point, normal operating range, "
      "characterization range, final classification and study type. {#tbl-params}")
```

The characterization range is the knowledge space edge for each parameter and is not itself
a proven acceptable range; the ranges that were derived from the data are reported later
(§7). Coded factor letters are used throughout the effect and coefficient tables, and
@tbl-legend maps them to the parameters.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.factor_legend_df(UO))
print()
print(": Coded factor legend for the screening and response-surface designs. {#tbl-legend}")
```

Each range was set from a distinct argument. Protein load was studied from well below to
well above the set-point, spanning conditions from a lightly loaded column to a load
approaching the dynamic binding capacity of the resin, because the upper edge is where
breakthrough and elevated pool host cell protein are both expected. Elution buffer pH was
bounded below by the pH at which antibody precipitation becomes a risk in the pool and above
by the pH at which product recovery begins to fall, so the studied range brackets the whole
usable elution window. Load flow rate was studied over a range that halves and doubles the
residence time at the set-point. End of pool collect was studied from a conservative early
stop to a stop well into the trailing edge, which is the region where additional product
recovery competes with additional impurity carry-over.

## Screening design

The screening study was a two-level full factorial in the four multivariate factors,
augmented with centre points, giving `{python} f"{n_scr}"` runs in randomised order. A full
factorial in four factors estimates every main effect and every two-factor interaction free
of aliasing (resolution is not a constraint at this factor count), which is why no fractional
design was used. The purpose of the screening study
was to identify which factors are active on each response and in what direction, and the
design carries no quadratic terms, so it cannot detect curvature. The screening model is
therefore an identification model and not a predictive one. The design matrix and the
measured responses are given in Appendix A.

## Response-surface design

The response-surface study was a face-centred central composite design in the same four
factors, with axial points at the faces of the cube and centre-point replicates, giving
`{python} f"{n_rsm}"` runs. All four screening factors were carried forward. Two of them
were active on pool host cell protein (protein load and elution buffer pH) and two on step
yield, and retaining all four keeps the predictive model defined over the same region as the
knowledge space in @tbl-params. The
axial points at the face of the cube allow the quadratic terms to be estimated without
extending the design beyond the characterization ranges. The response-surface model is the
predictive model of this report and is the basis of the operating region in §6 and the
proven acceptable ranges in §7. The design matrix and the measured responses are given in
Appendix B.

## Univariate assessment

Operating temperature and bed height were assessed one factor at a time over the ranges in
@tbl-params and were not carried into either multivariate design. Neither parameter is a
factor of the response-surface model, so the operating region defined in §6 makes no claim
about them, and their ranges rest on the univariate assessment together with the operating
and packing controls for the step (SOP-2007 and SOP-2008). Both remain general process
parameters.

# Results

## Centre-point performance and reproducibility

The centre-point replicates of the response-surface design establish the pure-error term
against which every lack-of-fit test in this section is judged, and they separate the three
responses sharply. @tbl-center gives the mean, standard deviation and coefficient of
variation of each response over the replicates.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.center_cv_df(UO, "rsm"), floatfmt=".4g")
print()
print(": Centre-point performance of the response-surface design, over "
      "replicate runs executed at the set-point of every factor. {#tbl-center}")
```

Step yield is the most reproducible response, at a coefficient of variation of
`{python} f"{cv('step_yield'):.1f}"` %, and pool host cell protein follows at
`{python} f"{cv('pool_hcp_ng_mg'):.1f}"` %. Leached Protein A is the least precise by a wide
margin, at `{python} f"{cv('leached_protein_a_ppm'):.1f}"` % about a mean of
`{python} f"{cmean('leached_protein_a_ppm'):.2f}"` ppm. That figure is a property of the
attribute and its assay together, and §5.3 separates the two contributions. The screening
design was less reproducible on pool host cell protein than the response-surface design
(`{python} f"{cv('pool_hcp_ng_mg', 'screening'):.1f}"` % against
`{python} f"{cv('pool_hcp_ng_mg'):.1f}"` %), which is consistent with the smaller number of
replicates it carried.

## Screening: factor effects

The screening study identified two active factors on pool host cell protein and three on
step yield, and none on leached Protein A. @tbl-fit-scr summarises the fit of the screening
model to each response.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.fit_summary_df(UO, "screening"), floatfmt=".4g")
print()
print(": Screening-model fit summary for the three measured responses. {#tbl-fit-scr}")
```

Pool host cell protein is dominated by elution buffer pH and protein load (coded factors B
and A). Raising elution buffer pH across its range lowers pool host cell protein by
`{python} f"{abs(eff('pool_hcp_ng_mg', 'B')):,.0f}"` ng/mg, and raising protein load across
its range increases it by `{python} f"{eff('pool_hcp_ng_mg', 'A'):,.0f}"` ng/mg. A
significant interaction between the two was identified. No other term reaches significance,
and load flow rate is the smallest effect of the four. The largest effects are given in
@tbl-eff-hcp.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.screening_effects_df(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg", top=5), floatfmt=".4g")
print()
print(": Largest screening effects on pool host cell protein. Effects are expressed as the "
      "change in response across the full characterization range of the factor. {#tbl-eff-hcp}")
```

Step yield is dominated by end of pool collect, which raises yield by
`{python} pct(eff('step_yield', 'D'))` across its range. Protein load and load flow rate both
reduce yield, and their interaction is significant, which is the expected signature of a
capacity limit that only bites when a heavily loaded column is also run fast (§5.4). The
three main effects and the interaction are given in @tbl-eff-yield.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.screening_effects_df(UO, "step_yield", top=5), floatfmt=".4g")
print()
print(": Largest screening effects on step yield. {#tbl-eff-yield}")
```

Leached Protein A showed no significant effect from any factor or interaction. The screening
model is not significant as a whole
(p = `{python} f"{fit_scr['leached_protein_a_ppm']['p']:.2f}"`), its adjusted coefficient of
determination is negative, and the smallest p-value among the ten terms is
`{python} f"{lpa_scr_pmin:.2f}"`. The full effect table for this response is given in
Appendix C (@tbl-appC3). That null result was carried forward and not treated as an absence
of data, and §5.3 reports what the response-surface design added to it.

Effect magnitudes from the screening study are estimates over a design with no curvature
terms. Where the response-surface model resolves curvature, as it does for elution buffer pH
on pool host cell protein, the screening estimate of a main effect is an average over the
range and understates the local slope at one end of it. The values quoted in the remainder
of this report are therefore the response-surface estimates.

## Response-surface models

Two of the three responses are adequately modelled and one is not, and the distinction
governs how each is used in the rest of this report. @tbl-fit-rsm gives the fit of the
response-surface model to each response.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.fit_summary_df(UO, "rsm"), floatfmt=".4g")
print()
print(": Response-surface model fit summary for the three measured responses. {#tbl-fit-rsm}")
```

Pool host cell protein is well described. The model explains
`{python} f"{fit_rsm['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['R2']:.3f}"` of the variation with an adjusted value
of `{python} f"{fit_rsm['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['adjR2']:.3f}"`, and its predicted coefficient of
determination is `{python} f"{fit_rsm['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['predR2']:.3f}"`, which is close
enough to the adjusted value to support prediction rather than description alone. The
lack-of-fit test is not significant at the 5 % level
(p = `{python} f"{fit_rsm['pool_hcp_ng_mg']['p_lof']:.3f}"`), although the margin is narrow,
so the quadratic form is accepted as adequate while the model is not extrapolated beyond the
characterization ranges. The coefficient table is given in @tbl-coef-hcp and the analysis of
variance in @tbl-anova-hcp.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.rsm_coeff_df(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg"), floatfmt=".4g")
print()
print(": Response-surface coefficients for pool host cell protein, on coded factors. "
      "{#tbl-coef-hcp}")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.anova_lof_df(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg"))  # auto format: sums of squares stay plain, p-values stay scientific
print()
print(": Analysis of variance for the pool host cell protein model, with the residual "
      "partitioned into lack of fit and centre-point pure error. {#tbl-anova-hcp}")
```

Four terms carry the pool host cell protein surface. Elution buffer pH and protein load are
the two large main effects and act in opposite directions. Their interaction is significant,
so the benefit of raising elution pH is larger at high load than at low load. The quadratic
term in elution buffer pH is significant and positive, so the response flattens as elution pH
approaches the top of its range (@fig-contours). End of pool collect carries a small
significant negative main effect that the screening design did not resolve. Pool host cell
protein is expressed
per unit of product mass, and collecting further into the trailing edge adds product mass to
the denominator, which is consistent with the yield result for the same factor.

Step yield is adequately modelled, at a coefficient of determination of
`{python} f"{fit_rsm['step_yield']['R2']:.3f}"` and an adjusted value of
`{python} f"{fit_rsm['step_yield']['adjR2']:.3f}"`, with no significant lack of fit
(p = `{python} f"{fit_rsm['step_yield']['p_lof']:.2f}"`). Its predicted coefficient of
determination is `{python} f"{fit_rsm['step_yield']['predR2']:.3f}"`, which is materially
lower than the adjusted value, so the model is used to describe the direction and rough size
of yield changes and not to predict a single run. End of pool collect remains the dominant
term, protein load and load flow rate remain negative, and the interaction between load and
flow rate remains significant. The coefficient table is in Appendix C.

No process parameter had a significant effect on leached Protein A. The response-surface
model is not significant as a whole
(p = `{python} f"{fit_rsm['leached_protein_a_ppm']['p']:.2f}"`), its adjusted coefficient of
determination is `{python} f"{fit_rsm['leached_protein_a_ppm']['adjR2']:.3f}"`, and its
predicted coefficient of determination is
`{python} f"{fit_rsm['leached_protein_a_ppm']['predR2']:.3f}"`. A negative predicted
coefficient of determination means the fitted surface predicts a held-out run less well than
the mean of the response does. The lack-of-fit test is not significant
(p = `{python} f"{fit_rsm['leached_protein_a_ppm']['p_lof']:.2f}"`), so the residual
variation is consistent with pure error and there is no evidence of structure the quadratic
form has missed. One term (the quadratic in elution buffer pH) reaches nominal significance,
and among the fourteen terms tested at the 5 % level that is what chance alone produces, so
no weight is placed on it.

The variation that is present in this response is analytical and resin-derived. The
centre-point replicates give a coefficient of variation of
`{python} f"{cv('leached_protein_a_ppm'):.1f}"` % for leached Protein A, against
`{python} f"{cv('pool_hcp_ng_mg'):.1f}"` % for pool host cell protein over the same four
runs. The leached Protein A assay (AMV-3016) has a precision of
`{python} f"{lpa_prec:.1f}"` % and accounts for `{python} f"{100 * lpa_varfrac:.0f}"` % of
the observed variance in this response. The remainder is run-to-run variation in ligand
release from the resin itself, which is governed by the resin life cycle (packing, cycle
number and sanitisation) and is controlled under SOP-2008.

This is a robustness result and it is reported as one. The response-surface model for leached
Protein A is retained in the knowledge space as evidence that the attribute does not depend
on protein load, elution buffer pH, load flow rate or end of pool collect over the ranges
studied, and it is not used as a predictive model. No claim in §6 rests on it. The operative
result for this attribute is the direct one: all `{python} f"{n_pools}"` pools assayed across
the screening and response-surface designs met the acceptance criterion of
`{python} f"{lpa_acc_hi:g}"` ppm, and the highest single determination was
`{python} f"{lpa_obs_max:.2f}"` ppm.

Diagnostics for the two responses that carry the argument are given in @fig-diag-hcp and
@fig-diag-lpa. For pool host cell protein the residuals show no structure against the
predicted value, the normal quantile plot is close to linear, and the actual against
predicted plot lies on the identity line across the whole range of the response. For leached
Protein A the residuals are equally free of structure, but the actual against predicted plot
shows the predicted values compressed into a narrow band while the observations scatter
across a much wider one, which is the visual form of a model with nothing to fit.

```{python}
#| label: fig-diag-hcp
#| fig-cap: "Model diagnostics for the pool host cell protein response-surface model: standardised residuals against predicted value, normal quantile plot, and actual against predicted."
fig = D.fig_diagnostics(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-diag-lpa
#| fig-cap: "Model diagnostics for the leached Protein A response-surface model. The compressed spread of predicted values against the observed spread is the signature of a response with no active factor."
fig = D.fig_diagnostics(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm")
plt.show()
```

## Mechanistic interpretation

The surfaces confirm the mechanistic expectations set out in §3.1, with one refinement. The
predicted responses over protein load and elution buffer pH, with the other two factors at
their set-points, are shown in @fig-contours.

```{python}
#| label: fig-contours
#| fig-cap: "Response-surface predictions over protein load and elution buffer pH, with load flow rate and end of pool collect held at their set-points. Panels are pool host cell protein, step yield and leached Protein A."
fig = D.fig_rsm_contours(UO, "load", "elution_ph")
plt.show()
```

Pool host cell protein varies over an order of magnitude across the characterization region.
At the set-point the model predicts `{python} f"{hcp_sp:,.0f}"` ng/mg. At the corner that
combines the highest protein load with the lowest elution buffer pH (the worst case for this
response) it predicts `{python} f"{hcp_worst:,.0f}"` ng/mg, and at the opposite corner
`{python} f"{hcp_best:,.0f}"` ng/mg. Against a nominal clarified-harvest burden of
`{python} f"{feed_hcp:,.0f}"` ng/mg, the step delivers
`{python} f"{hcp_lrv_sp:.2f}"` log reduction of host cell protein at the set-point and
`{python} f"{hcp_lrv_worst:.2f}"` log at that worst corner. Both directions follow from the
adsorption mechanism. Host cell protein enters the pool by co-adsorption to the resin and to
the product, so it rises with the mass of product bound, and it is released preferentially at
the harsher low-pH desorption condition. The interaction has the same origin: at low load
there is spare ligand capacity and the pH of desorption matters less, while at high load the
elution condition determines how much of the co-adsorbed impurity comes off with the product.

The curvature in elution buffer pH is the refinement prior knowledge did not supply. The
positive quadratic term flattens the surface as elution pH rises, so the reduction in pool
host cell protein per unit of pH is largest at the acidic end of the range and diminishes
towards the top of it. Desorption of the weakly bound impurity is close to complete at the
low end and the remaining impurity is more tightly associated, so further raising the elution
pH buys progressively less. Operating above the set-point therefore gains less than a linear
reading of the screening effect would suggest.

Step yield behaves as a capacity and recovery balance. Collecting further into the trailing
edge recovers product that would otherwise be lost to the strip, which is the dominant term.
Protein load and load flow rate each reduce yield by shortening the effective residence time
per unit of product presented to the resin, and their significant interaction reflects that
the two act on the same quantity. At the corner combining the highest load, the highest flow
rate and the earliest pool stop, the model predicts a step yield of
`{python} pct(yld_worst)`, against `{python} pct(yld_sp)` at the set-point.

These interactions are the reason the operating region is defined multivariately and not as a
set of independent ranges. The acceptable elution pH depends on the protein load, and the
acceptable load flow rate depends on the load, so a set of one-dimensional ranges would
either be too wide at one corner or needlessly narrow everywhere else.

# Design space

The design space for this step is the multivariate region in protein load, elution buffer pH,
load flow rate and end of pool collect over which the quality attribute the step sets remains
within its acceptance criterion, and that condition is met across the whole characterized
region. Every setting in the region studied delivers leached Protein A within its acceptance
criterion, whether the other factors are held at set-point or allowed to vary within their
normal operating ranges. The characterized region is therefore not constrained by the
attribute this step sets.

What does bound the operating region is the pool host cell protein handed forward. Over the
normal operating ranges of the four parameters the model predicts pool host cell protein
between `{python} f"{hcp_nor_lo:,.0f}"` and `{python} f"{hcp_nor_hi:,.0f}"` ng/mg, and step
yield between `{python} pct(yld_nor_lo)` and `{python} pct(yld_nor_hi)`. The worst case the
region must satisfy is the corner at maximum protein load and minimum elution buffer pH,
where pool host cell protein is highest and the load presented to cation exchange is
correspondingly highest. That corner is inside the characterized region and was executed in
both designs (@tbl-appA and @tbl-appB).

The pool host cell protein level is not judged against the drug-substance specification at
the outlet of this step, and no such claim is made here. Since cation exchange (PCR-007) and
anion exchange (PCR-008) reduce host cell protein to consistent levels well below the
drug-substance limit, the acceptable pool host cell protein from capture is linked to the
operating conditions of those two steps, and the cumulative position is consolidated in
PCMR-001. The role of this report is to quantify what the capture step delivers across its
region, which @fig-contours and @tbl-coef-hcp do.

The normal operating range of each parameter sits inside the characterized region, which in
turn sits inside the knowledge space bounded by the characterization ranges in @tbl-params.
Movement within the design space is not a change from a regulatory filing perspective under
ICH Q8(R2) [@ichq8], although any planned movement is assessed prospectively under the
quality system in line with ICH Q10 [@ichq10]. Operation outside the characterized region
requires change control and, where the mechanism is not already covered, new data.

Three bounds apply to this claim. The models cover the four multivariate parameters over the
ranges in @tbl-params and cover no other parameter (operating temperature and bed height in
particular). All runs used a single clarified-harvest pool at nominal titre and impurity
burden, so the region is defined for that feed state and the study does not bound the effect
of feed variability. The region is defined on the qualified scale-down model and is not
confirmed at commercial scale at its edges.

# Proven acceptable ranges

The acceptance criteria applied in this section are the study drug-substance specifications
for the two impurity attributes the step governs. For pool host cell protein the criterion is
the drug-substance limit of `{python} f"{hcp_acc_hi:g}"` ng/mg, and for leached Protein A it
is `{python} f"{lpa_acc_hi:g}"` ppm. Step yield is a process performance attribute with no
acceptance criterion of this kind and is not carried in the proven acceptable range analysis.
Two analyses were run for every combination of attribute and parameter, the first with the
other three factors held at their set-points and the second with those factors varying within
their normal operating ranges, propagated by Monte-Carlo simulation of the fitted
response-surface model. The second analysis is the robustness form and is the reproducible
default. Both are given below (@tbl-par).

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.par_table(UO))
print()
print(": Proven acceptable ranges by governed attribute and parameter, at set-point and "
      "with the remaining factors propagated across their normal operating ranges. {#tbl-par}")
```

The drug-substance criterion for host cell protein does not apply at the outlet of this step,
which is why @tbl-par carries no proven acceptable range in any of its pool host cell protein
rows. Host cell protein is a release attribute of the drug substance, and the drug substance
does not exist until after anion exchange. The measures that do apply to a capture step are
the clearance factor it delivers and the consistency of the load it hands to the polishing
steps. Both are given below for the nominal batch (@tbl-hcpchain).

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(hcp_chain.to_markdown(index=False, disable_numparse=True))
print()
print(": Host cell protein through the purification train for the nominal batch, with the "
      "clearance factor of each step and the document that reports it. {#tbl-hcpchain}")
```

Capture reduces host cell protein by a factor of `{python} f"{hcp_pa_fold:,.0f}"` from the
clarified harvest, which is the largest single reduction in the train. Cation exchange
(PCR-007) removes a further factor of `{python} f"{hcp_cex_fold:.0f}"` and anion exchange
(PCR-008) a further `{python} f"{hcp_aex_fold:.1f}"`, at which point the level is
`{python} f"{hcp_aex_out:.1f}"` ng/mg against the drug-substance limit of
`{python} f"{hcp_acc_hi:g}"` ng/mg. The limit is met after anion exchange and not before.
Since cation exchange and anion exchange reduce host cell protein to consistent levels well
below that limit, the acceptable pool host cell protein from capture is linked to the
operating conditions of those two steps, and the cumulative position is consolidated in
PCMR-001.

What this study contributes is the quantified dependence of the capture pool level on the
operating point, reported in §5.3 and §5.4. Over the normal operating ranges the fitted model
predicts pool host cell protein between `{python} f"{hcp_nor_lo:,.0f}"` and
`{python} f"{hcp_nor_hi:,.0f}"` ng/mg, a spread of about
`{python} f"{hcp_nor_hi / hcp_nor_lo:.1f}"`-fold, and the polishing steps are characterized
against a load within that band. The same analysis is shown for the governing parameter in
@fig-par-hcp, in the form used for the other attribute. No region is shaded in either panel,
because the predicted response lies above the drug-substance limit across the whole range of
elution buffer pH.

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-hcp
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range analysis for pool host cell protein against elution buffer pH, at set-point and with the remaining factors propagated across their normal operating ranges. The drawn limit is the drug-substance criterion, which does not apply at the outlet of this step, so no acceptable region is shaded."
fig = D.fig_par(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg", D.governing_factor(UO, "pool_hcp_ng_mg"))
plt.show()
```

Leached Protein A gives the opposite result. Its whole characterization range is proven
acceptable for every parameter at set-point, and the propagation across the normal operating
ranges narrows only one of them. For elution buffer pH the propagated range stops at
`{python} f"{lpa_par_ph:.2f}"` instead of the top of the characterization range, because the
upper tail of the predictive distribution reaches the acceptance criterion there. That bound
comes from the quadratic term discussed in §5.3, which is the only term in the model to reach
nominal significance and which the study does not regard as established. It is retained
because the analysis is run the same way for every response, and it is conservative. It also
lies well above the upper edge of the normal operating range for elution buffer pH. The
analysis for protein load (@fig-par-lpa), the governing parameter for this attribute, shows
the acceptable region covering the whole characterization range in both panels.

```{python}
#| label: fig-par-lpa
#| fig-cap: "Proven acceptable range analysis for leached Protein A against protein load, at set-point and with the remaining factors propagated across their normal operating ranges. The acceptable region covers the whole characterization range in both panels."
fig = D.fig_par(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm", D.governing_factor(UO, "leached_protein_a_ppm"))
plt.show()
```

The relationship between these ranges and the design space in §6 is a matter of dimension.
The proven acceptable ranges are one-dimensional statements about a single parameter, taken
either at set-point or with the other factors moving within their ranges, whereas the design
space is
the multivariate region in all four parameters at once. Where the whole characterization
range of a parameter is proven acceptable, as it is for leached Protein A, the binding
constraint on the operating region is not that parameter's univariate range. For this step
the binding constraint is the multivariate pool host cell protein corner identified in §6,
and it is set by the requirements of the downstream polishing steps.

Both analyses are bounded by the fitted model and by the characterization ranges. Neither
extends to feed states other than the one studied, and neither covers operating temperature
or bed height.

# Process capability and robustness

Commercial-scale capability was estimated from a Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{n_mc:,}"` batches with every parameter of the process train varying within its
normal operating range. The result for the three attributes this step governs, at drug
substance, is given below (@tbl-cap).

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cap_step, floatfmt=".4g")
print()
print(": Commercial-scale capability at drug substance for the quality attributes governed "
      "by the Protein A step. {#tbl-cap}")
```

Host cell protein is the tightest of the three, at a one-sided capability index of
`{python} f"{cpk_hcp:.2f}"`, with a simulated mean of
`{python} f"{hcp_ds_mean:.1f}"` ng/mg against a limit of
`{python} f"{hcp_acc_hi:g}"` ng/mg. That margin is the combined result of three clearance
steps and not of this one. Capture delivers `{python} f"{hcp_lrv_sp:.2f}"` log of the
reduction at the set-point, and the remainder comes from cation exchange (PCR-007) and anion
exchange (PCR-008). Residual DNA clears with a wider margin, at a capability index of
`{python} f"{cpk_dna:.2f}"`, and this step is credited with
`{python} f"{dna_lrv:.1f}"` log of DNA clearance, established by spiked clearance runs
outside the multivariate design and verified at drug substance by quantitative polymerase
chain reaction (AMV-3014).

Leached Protein A reaches drug substance at a mean of
`{python} f"{lpa_ds_mean:.4f}"` ppm against the acceptance criterion of
`{python} f"{lpa_acc_hi:g}"` ppm. The capability index for this attribute is very large and
carries no discriminating information, because the mean is orders of magnitude below the
limit. The informative statement is the clearance: the capture pool carries
`{python} f"{cmean('leached_protein_a_ppm'):.2f}"` ppm at the set-point, and the downstream
train removes about `{python} f"{lpa_ds_clear:.1f}"` log of it. Cation exchange and anion
exchange carry that reduction and report it in PCR-007 and PCR-008.

None of these capabilities is the limiting one for the drug substance. The minimum capability
index across all attributes of the process is `{python} f"{min_cpk:.2f}"`, and it belongs to
a viral clearance attribute characterized in PCR-008 and PCR-009. The capability figures in
@tbl-cap are conditioned on operation within the normal operating ranges of every parameter
of the train and on the scale-down models used to derive the underlying response models.
They are not a statement about operation at the edges of the characterized region.

# Parameter classification

Every parameter of the step was classified under the decision logic in SOP-4001, from the
effects demonstrated in §5 and from the risk of the parameter leaving its range in routine
operation. The classifications are carried in @tbl-params and the reasoning for each is
given below.

- Protein load is a well-controlled critical process parameter. It carries the second
  largest effect on pool host cell protein and a significant negative effect on step yield,
  so it is linked to a quality attribute of the drug substance. It is set by the mass loaded
  onto a column of known volume, which is directly measured and readily controlled, so the
  risk of operating outside the design space is low.
- Elution buffer pH is a well-controlled critical process parameter. It carries the largest
  single effect on pool host cell protein and interacts with protein load. It is controlled
  by buffer preparation and confirmed by release testing before use, which is a measurement
  with an established limit, so the risk of an undetected excursion is low (see DEV-005-01).
- Load flow rate is a key process parameter. It had no significant effect on either quality
  attribute in scope and a small negative effect on step yield, which places it in process
  performance and not in product quality.
- End of pool collect is a key process parameter. It carries the largest effect on step yield
  and a small significant effect on pool host cell protein through the normalisation of that
  response to product mass. It has no effect on the attribute this step sets, and the pool
  host cell protein it influences is not judged against a step-level criterion, so it does
  not meet the definition of a critical process parameter.
- Operating temperature is a general process parameter. It was not a factor of the
  multivariate design, it is held within a narrow band by the chromatography chamber, and
  RA-001 ranked it below the threshold for multivariate study.
- Bed height is a general process parameter. It is fixed at column packing under SOP-2008 and
  verified before use (plate count and peak asymmetry), so it is not an operating variable in
  routine manufacture.

No parameter of this step required designation as a critical process parameter. That
conclusion rests on two findings taken together. The only quality attribute the step sets is
insensitive to all four multivariate parameters over the ranges studied, and the attribute
that does respond strongly to them is one whose drug-substance level is set by later steps.
The drug-substance process carries `{python} f"{n_cpp_train}"` critical process parameter in
total, at the low-pH viral inactivation step, and it is reported in PCR-006. The two factors
with no significant effect on any quality attribute were classified and retained in the
knowledge space, because their demonstrated inactivity is the evidence that supports the
width of their ranges.

# Contribution to the control strategy

The Protein A step contributes four elements to the drug-substance control strategy, and each
follows from a result in §5.

Protein load and elution buffer pH are controlled within the normal operating ranges in
@tbl-params, as the two parameters linked to a quality attribute. Elution buffer pH is
additionally controlled at source: every elution buffer lot is released against a pH
acceptance limit before use, and a lot outside that limit is not released. The sensitivity
that justifies this control is quantified in the deviation record (§13). Load flow rate and
end of pool collect are
controlled within their ranges as key process parameters, to keep step yield and pool volume
consistent, and they are monitored batch to batch as process attributes.

Pool host cell protein and leached Protein A are monitored on every batch as in-process
attributes of the capture pool. Their function is trend detection and not acceptance, since
neither is judged against the drug-substance specification at this step, and both are
reported at drug substance under the release testing that supports PCMR-001. The resin is
controlled through its life cycle under SOP-2008 (packing qualification, sanitisation and a
maximum cycle number), which is the control that governs leached Protein A given the null
result reported above (§5.3).

The step's contribution to impurity clearance is credited as follows. Capture delivers
`{python} f"{hcp_lrv_sp:.2f}"` log of host cell protein reduction and
`{python} f"{dna_lrv:.1f}"` log of DNA reduction at the set-point, and the drug-substance
levels of both are achieved with cation exchange (PCR-007) and anion exchange (PCR-008). The
step does not by itself assure any drug-substance impurity limit. It makes no viral clearance
claim and no aggregate clearance claim, and it does not modify the glycan or charge-variant
attributes formed in the bioreactor (PCR-003). The cumulative position across all steps is
consolidated in PCMR-001.

# Discussion

The step is well understood, and the understanding is asymmetric across the three responses
in a way that is useful. Pool host cell protein has a predictive model over the four
multivariate parameters, so the impurity burden handed to the polishing steps can be
predicted from the operating point. Step yield has an adequate descriptive model that
identifies the corner where recovery falls. Leached Protein A has no model, and that is the
result rather than a gap in the study, because the attribute the step sets does not respond
to the parameters the step controls.

The robustness of leached Protein A deserves its bounds stated plainly. The finding holds
over the characterization ranges of the four multivariate parameters, on a single resin lot
family operated within the cycle limits of SOP-2008, and with the assay (AMV-3016)
contributing `{python} f"{100 * lpa_varfrac:.0f}"` % of the observed variance. It does not
extend to a
different resin, and RA-004 has already determined that a resin change would require
independent characterization with no bridging from platform data. It also does not extend
beyond the cycle limit, since ligand release is known to increase with cycle number and cycle
number was held constant here.

Confidence in the scale-down model is high for the effects this study reports and is limited
by design. Residence time, column volumes and bed height are matched between scales, so the
adsorption and desorption effects that drive every result in §5 transfer. Effects that would
arise from packing heterogeneity at scale, from wall support or from flow distribution across
the column diameter are not reproduced, and no claim in this report depends on them. The models predict mean levels and
carry no interval of their own, which is why the proven acceptable range analysis in §7 uses
a propagated predictive distribution and not the fitted mean alone.

Two deviations were recorded and both were retained after impact assessment. The first was a
buffer preparation error caught by release testing before the material reached a column, and
the second was an analytical result that could not be confirmed either way, dispositioned
conservatively by retaining the original determination. Neither changed a parameter
classification, an effect estimate or the operating region. Both are described in §13.

The principal limitations of the study are three. All runs used one clarified-harvest feed
state, so the study bounds the effect of the operating parameters and not of feed
variability; the A-Mab platform history supports robustness to feed variation, but this study
does not add to it. The operating region is defined on a laboratory-scale model and is not
confirmed at commercial scale at its edges. Resin cycle number was held constant, so the
life-cycle contribution to leached Protein A is controlled by SOP-2008 and validated
separately, and it is not characterized here.

# Conclusions

The Protein A capture step is well characterized and robust across the ranges studied. A
response-surface model over the four multivariate parameters predicts pool host cell protein
across the characterized region, and a second model describes step yield. Leached Protein A,
the only quality attribute the step sets, showed no dependence on any of the four parameters,
and all `{python} f"{n_pools}"` pools assayed met the acceptance criterion of
`{python} f"{lpa_acc_hi:g}"` ppm.

The operating region is defined multivariately, with the normal operating ranges of
@tbl-params nested inside it. `{python} f"{n_wccpp}"` parameters are well-controlled critical
process parameters, `{python} f"{n_kpp}"` are key process parameters and
`{python} f"{n_gpp}"` are general process parameters, and no parameter required designation
as a critical process parameter. At drug substance the three impurity attributes the step
governs meet their limits, with host cell protein the tightest at a capability index of
`{python} f"{cpk_hcp:.2f}"`.

The step makes no viral clearance claim, no aggregate clearance claim, and no claim that it
delivers any drug-substance impurity limit on its own. The `{python} f"{n_dev}"` recorded
deviations were resolved without changing any classification or the operating region. The
step is ready for Stage 2 at the ranges in @tbl-params, and this report rolls up into
PCMR-001.

## DEV-005-01 — elution buffer prepared below target

An elution buffer lot (LOT-BUF-5290) was prepared for a response-surface run and released at
pH `{python} f"{dev_005_01_ph_measured:.2f}"`, below its preparation target and below the
lower edge of the normal operating range for elution buffer pH. The magnitude matters at this
step more than it would elsewhere, because elution buffer pH is the largest single effect on
pool host cell protein. Had the lot been used with the other factors at their set-points, the
fitted model predicts a pool host cell protein of
`{python} f"{hcp_at_dev_ph:,.0f}"` ng/mg against `{python} f"{hcp_sp:,.0f}"` ng/mg at target,
a factor of `{python} f"{dev_ph_ratio:.2f}"`.

The deviation was detected at buffer release testing, before the lot was issued to the
column. Investigation by the buffer preparation area identified an endpoint error during
titration as the root cause, with no equipment fault and no other lot affected. The
non-conforming lot was rejected, a replacement lot was prepared and released within its pH
acceptance limit, and the affected run was executed with the replacement.

The impact on the study is therefore none. No non-conforming buffer reached a column, and the
run in question was executed at the elution pH assigned to it in the design, which is the
value shown in Appendix B (@tbl-appB). The affected run and its data were retained. The
corrective action was a revision to the buffer preparation record requiring a second
independent pH verification before release (SOP-2103). The deviation also confirms the value
of buffer pH release testing as a control-strategy element, and §10 records it as one.

## DEV-005-02 — leached Protein A determination out of trend

One leached Protein A determination was flagged during analytical review as out of trend on
the high side against the other runs of the same design. Analytical Development investigated
the plate record and identified suspected carryover from an adjacent high-concentration well
as the most likely cause, but the plate layout and the wash record could not establish it.
The retained aliquot of the same pool was re-assayed by the same validated method (AMV-3016)
and returned
`{python} f"{dev_005_02_retest_ppm:.1f}"` ppm, below the centre-point mean of
`{python} f"{cmean('leached_protein_a_ppm'):.2f}"` ppm and well below the acceptance
criterion of `{python} f"{lpa_acc_hi:g}"` ppm.

Because carryover was suspected but not confirmed, the original determination could not be
invalidated, and it was retained in the reported data set. The disposition is deliberately
conservative, because the higher of the two determinations is the one carried into every
model and every table in §5. The re-assay was recorded in the analytical investigation and
was not substituted for the original.

The deviation is consistent with the assay behaviour reported in §5.3. The leached Protein A
method has a precision of `{python} f"{lpa_prec:.1f}"` % and a limit of quantitation of
`{python} f"{lpa_loq:g}"` ppm, and it accounts for
`{python} f"{100 * lpa_varfrac:.0f}"` % of the observed variance in this response. A single
determination that separates from the others by more than the method's repeatability is
expected at that variance, and it is one of the reasons the study does not read a factor
effect into the leached Protein A surface. No classification, effect estimate or acceptance
conclusion changed as a result. The corrective action was a revision to the plate layout in
the analytical method record, placing a wash well between samples of widely different
concentration.
